A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JUICE research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original intervention experiments across six language models, mechanistic analyses, and robustness evaluations, including Tables 3–7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments varying the number of intervened heads and scaling factors in Figure 5b–c.

M1.justification: JUICE retains the same head selection, consistency filtering, activation caching, and dual-run intervention procedure. Appendix E corrects head-index notation and clarifies score initialization without changing the procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six factual domains, NQ-Swap, and four MemoTrap tasks, retaining clean, substitution-conflict, coherent-conflict, and paraphrased inputs. The added sensitivity experiments use the existing World Capital coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Original, Prompt, PH3l, PH3s, and JUNE, with CAD additionally evaluated for contextual reliance. Newly cited related methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: New sensitivity protocols sweep K from 1 to 30 and positive/negative scaling magnitudes from 0 to 5 in 0.5 increments, using Gemma and average accuracy across three World Capital conflict types (Section 4.3; Appendix D.3). Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 5b–c adds focused sensitivity analyses of head count and scaling factors. The existing head-selection-set-size analysis, paraphrase robustness experiment, and single-run versus dual-run ablation are retained, making this a limited extension of the robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions describe sample standard deviations for the component-knockout plots in Appendix D.1. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 5b newly reports accuracy of at least 85% throughout the tested head-count range, and Figure 5c adds the scaling-factor response surface. Numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are unchanged; these are additional sensitivity results, not improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same mathematical setups, assumptions, propositions, derivations, and proofs. The new task diagram and Appendix G.2's acknowledgment of loose logit/probability terminology do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: CP superposition, training-free steering toward either knowledge source, strong performance across 11 datasets and six architectures, and a theoretical explanation of JUICE.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 1 correct the interpretation from context heads becoming memory heads to memory heads becoming context heads, retaining the same ablation measurements. Section 4.3 extends the robustness interpretation to the new sweeps. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a curated-dataset access link in Section 2.1, clarifies head-index membership and zero-initialized score dictionaries in the pseudocode, and identifies the Delta computing resource in acknowledgments. The existing code link and primary hyperparameter settings are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds references to IRCAN (Shi et al., 2024a) and Jin et al. (2025) on contextual-knowledge mechanisms. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works; the paper's overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 is expanded and Appendix D.3 rewritten to explain the additional sensitivity studies. There are localized terminology, algorithm-reference, and model-name corrections, plus acknowledgments and publication information. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual explanation expands substantially through new diagrams of CP superposition and the theoretical tasks (Figures 1 and 7). v1's standalone appendix robustness plot becomes Figure 5a in a main-text three-panel display with two new panels. Existing figures and tables are retained, with several relocated.

improvement.justification: The added Gemma/World Capital sensitivity studies extend v1's limited hyperparameter checks and strengthen support for robustness. Corrected head labels and pseudocode, explanatory diagrams, and the dataset link improve clarity and reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains; the core method, benchmark comparisons, and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
